title: The Gang's Back, the Poster's 60 Feet Tall, and Arshad Warsi Promises It's Funny Again
excerpt: Dhamaal 4 unveils its trailer at an amusement park waterfall, dodges Christopher Nolan's Odyssey by moving up a week, and bets everything on a return to the original's anarchic innocence.
body:
Picture this: a 60-foot poster cascading down the Grand Waterfall at Imagicaa, water crashing over **Ajay Devgn**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, and **Jaaved Jaaferi**'s oversized faces while the cast stands below, grinning like men who know exactly what they've got. That was the **Dhamaal 4** trailer launch — and if the venue choice feels a little extra, well, that's the franchise in a nutshell.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

The fourth instalment of Bollywood's most lovably chaotic comedy series drops in theatres on **July 10, 2026**, with the original gang intact and a promise from one of its stars that nearly made the internet exhale in relief.

> "The innocence which the original Dhamaal had is back with Dhamaal 4." — Arshad Warsi

If you've been a Dhamaal fan since the 2007 original — the Goa airport chase, the "Jai Maharashtra" parachute scene, the sheer unhinged energy of four idiots chasing buried treasure — that sentence means everything. Because the franchise wobbled. **Double Dhamaal** (2011) leaned too hard into slapstick. **Total Dhamaal** (2019) brought in too many new faces and lost some of the original quartet's chemistry in the crowd. Warsi knows this. He knows what fans actually want.

## Back to the Beginning

Director **Indra Kumar** appears to have heard the feedback. Dhamaal 4 strips the cast back to its core: Devgn, Warsi, Deshmukh, and Jaaferi, supported by the reliably hilarious **Sanjay Mishra** and bolstered by new additions **Esha Gupta**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Anjali Anand**, **Upendra Limaye**, **Vijay Patkar**, and **Ravi Kishan**.

Warsi, reflecting on reuniting with the team, offered a quote that felt less like a press junket soundbite and more like a man talking about family:

> "Dhamaal gang is like a family to me. It is always good to collaborate with each one of them and this time we all are going to explode together in a much more larger way and take people on a laugh ride."

The BTS footage released alongside the trailer shows exactly this: Devgn breaking character mid-take, Warsi improvising bits that crack up the crew, Jaaferi doing something deeply physical and probably unsafe. It looks like a set where people are having fun, and that energy — when it translates to screen — is what made the original Dhamaal a cult classic.

## The Nolan Dodge

Here's a fun piece of industry chess: Dhamaal 4 was originally scheduled for **July 17**, but the makers quietly moved it up a week to **July 10**. The reason? **Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey** lands on July 17, and nobody in Bollywood wants to share a release frame with the man who turned Oppenheimer into a ₹90 crore opener in India.

The strategy is smart. Dhamaal 4 gets a clean opening week, free from the IMAX-hogging, premium-screen-dominating Nolan machine. By the time The Odyssey arrives, the comedy will have banked its first-week number and settled into its legs. It's the kind of calendar awareness that separates the producers who survive the modern box office from those who get crushed by it.

## Why the Franchise Still Matters

The Dhamaal series occupies a specific space in Indian pop culture: it's the comedy franchise that families actually agree on. Not too crude for parents. Not too tame for college kids. Not too smart for its own good. Just four deeply stupid men doing deeply stupid things, and the audience loving every second of it.

For diaspora audiences, the franchise carries particular nostalgia. The original Dhamaal was a DVD staple in NRI households. "Yeh Baburao ka style hai" became a catchphrase in dorm rooms from New Jersey to London. If you grew up Indian abroad in the 2000s, you've quoted this film at least once.

Dhamaal 4 is **releasing worldwide on July 10**, which means NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia should be able to catch it opening weekend. It's positioned as a family entertainer — the kind of film you take your parents to, or your kids, or both.

## The Competition

July 10 is crowded even without Nolan. Dhamaal 4 shares its date with the live-action **Moana** and **Evil Dead Burn** internationally. But in the Bollywood lane, it has a relatively clear road. **Alpha** (Alia Bhatt, Sharvari) releases on July 3, a full week earlier. The two films target different audiences entirely — spy action versus family comedy — so cannibalisation is unlikely.

The film sits at **#5 on IMDb's Most Anticipated Indian Movies of 2026**, behind Ramayana, Alpha, Toxic, and King. For a comedy sequel without a single A-list heroine in its cast, that's impressive. It tells you the franchise name alone is the draw.

Dhamaal 4 doesn't need to reinvent anything. It just needs to be what Arshad Warsi promised: innocent, chaotic, and funny. If the trailer is anything to go by, it's at least two of those three. July 10 will tell us if it's all of them.
